title: Khadijah's comfort
hookLine: she tells him Allah would never disgrace him: you keep ties, help the weak, honor guests (Bukhari)

cards: He comes down the mountain shaking. The hadith says his heart was trembling, and that he went straight to Khadijah and said: cover me, cover me. She wrapped him until the fear left.
Then he told her everything, and said he feared for himself. What she said next isn't a sermon, and it isn't an explanation. It's a list, and every item on it is something he did.

teach.b: Here's the answer, as Sahih al-Bukhari keeps it from 'Aishah. Never, by Allah. Allah would never disgrace you.
Then her reasons. You keep the ties of kinship. You carry the burden of the weak.
You give to those who have nothing. You honor your guest. And you stand by people when real trouble comes.
It's an odd kind of comfort. She doesn't explain the angel; she can't, and doesn't pretend to. She argues from evidence she has seen with her own eyes: how he treats people.
Her logic: a God who sees all that will not shame this man. Now the first item. The Arabic says he keeps the rahim, a word for the womb, used for the bonds of family.

teach.h: THE RAHIM, A BRANCH OF MERCY.
teach.b: A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says the rahim is a branch of ar-Rahman, the Merciful, and that whoever keeps it connected, Allah keeps connected. So the first thing she names is tied, in his own later words, to mercy.

teach.h: THE SAME LIST FOR ABU BAKR.
teach.b: Years later, when the Prophet's friend Abu Bakr was leaving Mecca under pressure, a chief named Ibn al-Daghinah stopped him, said a man like you should not be driven out, and gave almost the same list. Keeps ties.
Carries the weak. Gives to those with nothing. Honors guests.
Bukhari records both. The qualities Khadijah named weren't only a wife's praise; an outsider named them too.

how: Muslims retell Khadijah's words when speaking of good character and of keeping family ties, silat al-rahim, which the Qur'an and hadith treat as a duty and a mercy.

the cloak she wrapped him in on the mountain
her list of his good deeds when he came home afraid

games.q: your husband comes home shaking, afraid something is wrong with him. you can't explain what he saw. what do you say?
o: tell him it was only a dream.
remind him of the good he does, as evidence.
send for a soothsayer to explain it.
games.why: never, by Allah, she said: Allah would never disgrace you. then she listed his deeds, and later took him to her cousin Waraqa.

practice: Think of someone who's frightened, doubting themselves, or just tired, and do what Khadijah did: don't argue with the fear, list the evidence. Who do they show up for, feed, carry, welcome?
Make it three or four specific things, and if you pray, thank Allah for the good in them.

wordCard.voice: Khadijah's comfort. When he came home afraid, she told him Allah would never disgrace him, and named the good he did: ties kept, the weak carried, guests honored. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: keeping the ties of kinship, the first good she named.

carryVoice: Your line: allah would never disgrace you. Her comfort was a list of his deeds. See you tomorrow.
